seoTitle: How to Use Gemini AI with Google Workspace (2026)
metaDescription: Turn on Gemini inside Google Workspace's Admin console, fix the access setting that leaves some users without it, and find out where Veo video generation really lives.
intro:
Gemini shows up as an app icon next to Gmail and Docs in every Workspace account, but whether it works for your users depends on a setting most people never open: the Gemini app controls inside the Google Admin console.

This guide covers the real path — from the apps launcher where Gemini first appears, into the Admin console where an administrator sets service status and user access, and out to using the current Gemini model day to day. It also covers something a lot of 2026 guides still get wrong: video generation doesn't live inside the general Gemini panel. It's a separate feature of Google Vids, gated by its own plan rules.
prerequisites: A Google Workspace account with Admin console access, or an administrator on hand who can flip the settings below
costNote: The Gemini app ships included with most current Business, Enterprise, Education, and Frontline editions. Heavier reasoning and higher usage limits sit behind the separate AI Expanded Access add-on Google introduced in 2026. Video generation eligibility is edition-specific too: Google gave Business Starter, Enterprise Starter, and Nonprofit accounts temporary free access to Veo through Google Vids, running only through May 31, 2026. That window has since closed, so check current eligibility on Google's Workspace plan page instead of assuming it still applies.

steps.heading: Find Gemini in the Google apps launcher
steps.body:
Gemini sits in the grid from the nine-dot apps launcher in the top corner of any Google page, alongside Drive, Docs, Sheets, and, for admins, the Admin console itself. This is the fastest way to jump between the consumer-facing Gemini app and the Workspace admin tools without hunting through bookmarks.

If Gemini isn't in that grid at all, that's the first sign it hasn't been turned on for the account yet, which the next two steps fix.

image.caption: The Google apps launcher open on google.com, showing Gemini listed alongside Admin, Gmail, Drive, Docs, and Sheets.

steps.heading: Open Generative AI settings in the Admin console
steps.body: From the launcher, admins go into Admin, then Generative AI in the left-hand navigation. It expands into Gemini app, Gemini for Workspace, NotebookLM, and Gemini reports. Gemini app controls the standalone gemini.google.com experience; Gemini for Workspace governs the AI features embedded inside Docs, Sheets, and Gmail. They're configured separately, so check both if something works in one place and not the other.

steps.heading: Check the service status and user access
steps.body:
The Gemini app settings page opens on Service status, showing either On for everyone or a more restricted setting. This is the master switch: if it's off, nothing else on the page matters, since no one in the organization can reach Gemini regardless of their individual permissions. Changing it can take up to 24 hours to apply, though it's usually faster. Making this change requires the Gemini Settings administrator privilege.

Below Service status, the User access panel controls per-user rules — for example, whether access follows license assignment or is opened to everyone regardless of license. It's common to gate a new AI feature to a licensed group before rolling it out further, so if some users can't reach Gemini while the service itself is on, this panel is the next thing to check.

image.caption: The Gemini app settings screen in the Google Admin console, showing service status set to ON for everyone and a User access panel below it.

steps.heading: Confirm the licence behind the access toggle
steps.body: Because access is commonly tied to licence, confirm which Workspace edition each user is on before assuming a toggle is broken. Flipping User access to on for someone without the right licence attached won't produce a working Gemini app for that person; the licence has to be assigned first, and the deeper reasoning features behind AI Expanded Access need that add-on specifically.

steps.heading: Use the current model, and find Veo in the right place
steps.body:
Google rolled Gemini 3 Pro out to the Gemini app for Workspace customers in November 2025, selectable from the model dropdown; it's replaced the older Gemini 2.5 Pro that most 2026 guides still describe as current, and the update applies automatically without any per-user setup beyond the access already granted above.

Video generation is not part of that same panel. Veo lives specifically inside Google Vids: open the Generate video icon in the right sidebar of the Vids editor, choose Veo, and describe the clip. It's a different app with its own edition rules, which is why turning on Gemini elsewhere doesn't automatically make Veo appear.

troubleshooting.problem: Gemini is missing for the whole organization
troubleshooting.cause: Service status under Generative AI > Gemini app is set to off, or only recently switched on.
troubleshooting.fix: Set Service status to On for everyone and Save. Allow up to 24 hours for the change to reach every user, though it's typically quicker.

troubleshooting.problem: Service status is on, but some users still don't see Gemini
troubleshooting.cause: The User access setting is scoped to license, and those specific users don't have a qualifying Workspace edition assigned.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the User access panel and either assign the licence those users need or turn on access regardless of licence, if that fits the organization's rollout plan.

troubleshooting.problem: Veo video generation doesn't appear anywhere
troubleshooting.cause: Looking for it inside the Gemini side panel instead of Google Vids, or being on an edition whose temporary free access window (Business Starter, Enterprise Starter, Nonprofit, through May 31, 2026) has ended.
troubleshooting.fix: Open Google Vids directly and use the Generate video icon in the editor's right sidebar. If it's still missing, check current edition eligibility on Google's Workspace plans page instead of assuming last year's access still holds.

faq.question: Which Gemini model runs inside Workspace now?
faq.answer: Gemini 3 Pro, rolled out to the Gemini app for Workspace customers in November 2025 and selectable from the model dropdown. It replaced Gemini 2.5 Pro and updates automatically, so there's nothing to manually upgrade once Gemini app access is on.

faq.question: Is Gemini included in all Google Workspace plans?
faq.answer: It ships with most current Business, Enterprise, Education, and Frontline editions, but the Admin console's User access setting can still restrict it, and the heaviest reasoning limits sit behind the separate AI Expanded Access add-on.

faq.question: Where do I find Veo video generation?
faq.answer: Inside Google Vids, not the general Gemini panel. Open the Vids editor, use the Generate video icon in the right sidebar, and select Veo.

faq.question: Why can't some users see Gemini even though it's turned on?
faq.answer: Check the User access panel under Generative AI > Gemini app. Access can be scoped to a specific organizational unit or gated by licence instead of opened to everyone by default.

faq.question: My organization was on Business Starter and had free Veo access. Is that still active?
faq.answer: Google's own announcement scoped that free access, for Business Starter, Enterprise Starter, and Nonprofit accounts, through May 31, 2026. That date has passed, so check the current Workspace plans page instead of assuming it still applies.

faq.question: Do I need any special training to use Gemini in Workspace?
faq.answer: No. Once access is enabled, Gemini works through plain-language prompts inside the apps already in daily use.
